root_cause.text: In nf_tables `nft_add_set_elem()`, the set size check used `atomic_add_unless(&set->nelems, 1, max)` only after the element had already been inserted/published, so when the set was full the code removed the just-published element on the error path without an RCU grace period and without a transaction to safely unwind it.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE/commit states “In case that the set is full, a new element gets published then removed without waiting for the RCU grace period, while RCU reader can be walking over it already,” and the patch moves the `set->nelems` increment before insertion via `atomic_inc_return(&set->nelems)`, always allocates/adds the element transaction, returns `-ENFILE` through `set_full`, and deletes the old `err_set_full: nft_setelem_remove(...)` path.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a local set_full state flag in nft_add_set_elem() to support later handling of full-set conditions.
intent_record.what: A new local boolean variable named set_full is introduced in nft_add_set_elem() and initialized to false, with no other changes shown in this diff hunk.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this hunk alone does not change behavior directly, but it prepares the function to track whether the set has reached a full condition so later code in the function can branch on that state.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix set element accounting by incrementing non-catchall element counts before transaction creation, detecting over-capacity, and unwinding the count correctly on allocation failure.
intent_record.what: The change adds a conditional block before transaction allocation that skips elements marked with NFT_SET_ELEM_CATCHALL, otherwise reads the set maximum size, atomically increments set->nelems, and sets set_full to true when the incremented count exceeds the maximum; it also changes the error path for nft_trans_elem_alloc() failure from err_elem_free to err_set_size.
intent_record.how: At runtime, normal set element insertions now immediately update the set element count and detect when the set has exceeded its configured maximum size, while catchall elements are excluded from that accounting. Redirecting the allocation failure path to err_set_size ensures the new size/accounting state can be properly unwound instead of leaving the increment unhandled.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix nft_add_set_elem() to use the correct error cleanup path after queuing a transaction-added element, ensuring proper rollback of set state.
intent_record.what: In nft_add_set_elem(), the error-path jump after assigning ue->priv = elem_priv and calling nft_trans_commit_list_add_elem(ctx->net, trans) was changed from 'goto err_elem_free' to 'goto err_set_size'.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this changes which cleanup/error handling block executes when that branch is taken, so the function now follows the set-size rollback path instead of freeing the element directly, ensuring the appropriate state cleanup for a transaction-added element and avoiding incorrect error recovery.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix nftables set element size accounting by deferring full-set reporting and decrementing the element count on post-increment error paths.
intent_record.what: The patch removes the earlier pre-insertion size check that used nft_set_maxsize(set) and atomic_add_unless(&set->nelems, 1, max), deletes the err_set_full label that called nft_setelem_remove(), changes the success return to `return set_full ? -ENFILE : 0;`, and adds a new cleanup path `err_set_size` that decrements `set->nelems` with `atomic_dec(&set->nelems)` for non-catchall elements before destroying the element.
intent_record.how: Instead of rejecting the element before commit when the set appears full, the function now proceeds and returns -ENFILE only if `set_full` was detected after insertion logic. On failure paths after the element count has been incremented, it compensates by decrementing `set->nelems`, preventing the element counter from remaining artificially elevated and avoiding inconsistent set size accounting.

consistency_review.core_intent: Fix nftables set element accounting and capacity handling by adjusting when element counts are updated, deferring full-set checks, and correctly unwinding counts on error paths.

relevance_review.reason: This change directly targets full-set handling inside nft_add_set_elem(), which is the condition at the core of the bug. Adding a local set_full flag is part of tracking and safely handling the case where insertion occurs before the size check detects the set is full.

The changes directly address the faulty set-capacity/accounting logic in nft_add_set_elem(): they move and correct element count updates, defer full-set handling, and properly unwind counts on error paths, which matches the root cause of checking capacity too late after insertion/publication.

The change is in nft_add_set_elem() and specifically fixes the error cleanup/rollback path for a transaction-added element after it has been queued/published, which directly relates to the root cause of unsafe post-publication removal without proper transactional unwinding.

candidates.rationale: This is the core faulty capacity check. It increments/checks set size only after the element has already been inserted/published, so a full-set condition is detected too late and triggers unsafe rollback of a visible element.
When the late full-set check fails, control jumps to the cleanup path that unwinds an already published element, directly enabling the unsafe removal described in the root cause.
This removes the just-published element on the full-set error path without RCU grace period or transactional protection, which is the unsafe unwind highlighted in the root cause.

vuln_statements.explanation: This is the primary vulnerable statement. It performs the full-set capacity check only after the new element has already been inserted/published, so detecting a full set here is too late and forces rollback of an already visible element.

When the late capacity check fails, this transfers control to the full-set error path, causing unwind of an element that was already published, which is the unsafe behavior described in the root cause.
This statement removes the just-published element during error handling for the late full-set detection, without the needed RCU grace period or transactional protection.
